entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zhu Shuzhen was a Chinese poet of the Song dynasty, born in unknown circumstances and died in 1131. She married an official who treated her poorly, leading to either an affair or her suicide. Her poetry, which expressed her grief and longing, was destroyed by her parents after her death.

Zhu Shuzhen's life is significant because it highlights the limited options and harsh realities faced by women in ancient Chinese society. Her poetry, though lost, would have provided valuable insights into the experiences of women during this period.

Her legacy is complex, as it reflects the societal pressures that led to her tragic end. Despite this, her story serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving historical records and preserving the works of women who have been marginalized throughout history.

One striking statistic about Zhu Shuzhen is that she was one of the few women poets of the Song dynasty to have achieved recognition, despite the societal norms of the time.
